$comment-purpose: Flow's own self-configuration. Flow is a Claude Code plugin: mostly markdown + stdlib Python, with NO launchable app — hence platform=library, which makes /flow:verify-build self-skip (there is no runnable target to drive).
$comment-uiSurface: TRUE, deliberately. Flow has no app, but it DOES author and ship browser UI: the click-to-comment annotation overlay, the verify-build HTML report renderer, and the visual-history skeleton. Those render in a consumer's browser and a human interacts with them, so they are a UI surface and /flow:accessibility-review must audit them. This was `false` until v1.24.0, which meant flow's own most interactive artifact was the one file its a11y gate never looked at — a dogfooding blind spot, not a property of the code.
$comment-uiFilePatterns: Scoped to the files that actually emit browser UI, NOT a bare extension match — most of this repo is prose and stdlib Python, and a repo-wide pattern would make every docs PR read as a UI change. Single extended-regex string (consumed via jq -r then grep -E), never an array.
$comment-visualHistoryPath: Default is core-docs/visual-history.html, but CLAUDE.md reserves core-docs/ for the consumer template scaffolding — flow tracks itself in dev-docs/. Set explicitly so a visually-significant ship can't create a core-docs/ directory in this repo and cross the three-surface boundary.
$comment-verifyReportPath: Repo-local (gitignored) instead of the /tmp default, so the rendered report can be SERVED by the .claude/launch.json 'flow-report' recipe and driven in a browser. A /tmp path cannot be served without exposing the whole temp dir.
$comment-fragmented-docs: historyPath / feedbackPath / changelogPath point at DIRECTORIES, not files -- one file per entry (the towncrier/changesets pattern). This is the whole point: an append-only doc is the dominant source of merge conflicts, because every concurrent PR appends at the same insertion point. One file per entry removes the shared line, and it also removes a silent-deletion class -- a text merge can drop an entry with no conflict markers and a clean parse (it did: see changelog/README.md and the two preserved duplicates), but it cannot silently drop a FILE. There is deliberately NO committed rollup and NO committed index: either would recreate the exact conflict being removed, since every new entry would append a line to it. Readers resolve these slots through plugins/flow/lib/resolve-doc-slot.sh, which accepts file-or-directory so single-file consumers keep working unchanged.
$comment-behaviorBearingDocPatterns: Flow ships PROMPTS: a SKILL.md and an agents/*.md are deployed surface by CLAUDE.md's own rule that prompt changes are code changes. Without this slot /flow:audit-coverage was structurally blind to most of what this repo changes -- measured on #159, where all five undeclared behaviours lived in a SKILL.md the behaviour diff excluded, so its recorded 0-of-5 was never a judgment failure. `rules/` is included for THIS repo's dev-side .claude/rules/*.md, which do load into every session (verified: general.md is present in session context). Read that narrowly, and note what it is NOT: #170/FB-0124 retracted flow's broader claim that the four PLUGIN-SHIPPED rule-skills attach by path -- they are model-invoked, and a plugin cannot ship a rules/ directory at all (plugins/flow/rules/ does not exist; the four live under skills/ and are matched by the skills/ clause, not this one). So a consumer inherits this clause for their own .claude/rules/, not for anything flow ships. evals/ and fixtures/ stay excluded by the test-path filter: a fixture SKILL.md is not deployed surface.
$comment-flowRepoPath: Set 2026-09-26 (FB-0118) — flowRepoPath was UNSET, which per its own schema means '/flow:contribute disabled'. flow's own repo is the one place this slot should obviously point at itself, and leaving it unset meant the lesson-harvest drain has never once been runnable in-repo. CAVEAT this doc does not resolve: the value is an absolute path, so it is only correct for whichever machine/clone reads it. This one is a Conductor cloud-sandbox path (/home/vercel-sandbox/flow) — correct for cloud-worker checkouts using this convention, but WRONG on any local clone (e.g. a Mac dev checkout) until that machine sets its own. flowRepoPath is a machine-local override baked into a repo-shared file; a future fix might read an env var first. Flagged, not solved, here.
$comment-referenceGlob: REQUIRED here, and not cosmetic (FB-0082). The schema default is 'core-docs/*.md', which does not exist in this repo -- flow keeps reference docs in dev-docs/. Without this slot the /flow:critique-plan preprocessor resolved ZERO reference documents and injected no '## Reference documents' section at all, silently: the critic could cite no project rule, and the result was indistinguishable from 'there were no rules to violate'. critique-plan/SKILL.md has asserted "flow's own repo overrides to dev-docs/*.md" for several versions while this file did not; the claim was simply false. SECOND PATTERN ADDED when feedback.md was fragmented into dev-docs/feedback/: the FB corpus is a reference document (extract_session.py skips only history/plan/roadmap by name, NOT feedback), so moving it into a subdirectory would have dropped every FB rule out of `dev-docs/*.md` -- and the FB-0082 zero-resolution warning would NOT have fired, because README/spec/workflow/design-language still resolve. A quieter recurrence of the same bug, on the skill that catches it. NOT `dev-docs/**/*.md`, which would drag in the whole of handoffs/ and research/.
$comment-sensitivePaths: Flow's OWN gate machinery. Only the additions are listed: the schema's shape-based defaults (.env / auth / migrations / schemas / CI) are a FLOOR that is merged in, not replaced, so this list cannot accidentally narrow the policy. A wrong version in any of these fails SILENTLY -- a mis-classifying gate passes bad work -- so they never auto-approve at the plan gate and never route below the top tier at dispatch. The schema's defaults deliberately do NOT name these: ship/manifest-triage/skip-audit/verify-build are FLOW's filenames, and hardcoding them in the plugin would make its gate policy assume it was running on flow.
$comment-previewBackend: SET DELIBERATELY, and the reason is a shape this repo has paid for before (FB-0085): a feature whose slot is unset by default is a feature that runs nowhere and is never exercised, including here. previewBackend is off by default for consumers -- it has to be, since no host's CLI may be named in a plugin artifact -- so flow's OWN config is the one place that must name one. flow.config.json is PROJECT config, so a vendor name here is fine; the same name in plugins/flow/** would not be. `serve` calls .claude/bin/flow-preview-serve.sh because the adapter refuses a template carrying a shell operator, and backgrounding a server needs `&` and `>` -- so the backgrounding lives in a script the template CALLS, exactly as preview_backend.validate instructs. MEASURED 2026-10-04: an unauthenticated fetch of a served page returns http 401 'Sign in to view this preview.' (30 bytes) against a local control of http 200 (86 bytes) -- so the gate is real, not merely documented. Audience is the org (Conductor sign-in + workspace read access), NOT the public. PORT 8897, NOT 8899: `.claude/launch.json` serves `.flow` itself on 8899, and a server rooted at the scratch dir is exactly what must not be published. The root check in flow-preview-serve.sh is the real defence (any port can collide); a non-colliding default is belt-and-braces.

previewBackend.audience: anyone signed in to the host with read access to this workspace
